Figure 20 Greater than 5 ft of 4-layer ASL/ASL/AFL/GDC followed by > 10 ft of 3-layer ASL/AFL/GDC coating. 2.6 Q6: In Q6, substantial progress has been made in establishing the lamination window for the EEA utilizing the Fanny May mill at room temperature and at 100°C. Previous efforts had established the processing window for these temperature conditions on the BMF’s heated calender. The work indicates that the processing conditions can be translated from the BMF’s heated calender to the Fenn 4-High mill, either at room temperature or by preheating the sample prior to calendering. Samples were preheated under aluminum blocks in an oven until temperature equilibration, verified with an IR thermometer, then laminated in a single pass.. Demonstrating the lamination window is relevant between different 14 equipment and processing setups is of significant value, which can be transferred to the BMF’s R2R heated calender for optimal manufacturing process. EEAs were built up via lamination of layers to yield a stack (ASL/ASL/AFL/GDC) through various configurations, including: 1) single layer build up ASL+ASL  ASL/ASL + AFL  ASL/ASL/AFL + GDC, and pre-coated multiple layers lamination including: 2) ASL/ASL + AFL  ASL/ASL/AFL + GDC, 3) ASL/ASL + AFL/GDC and 4) ASL/ASL/AFL + GDC. Visual inspection appeared to show good contact between the layers for the laminations made at RT using Fenn May mill, SEM imaging, however, revealed delamination for the room temperature samples, primarily between the GDC and the AFL layers of the EEA. This was observed for all RT samples regardless of the configuration of their build. It might come from the difference of the binder and plasticizer composition between the GDC and the closely matching AFL and ASL coatings. The 7 × 7 in laminate prepared via lamination of the GDC to partial coated EEA at room temperature on the Fanny May mill and corresponding SEM are shown in Figure 21, with the delamination only apparent in SEM microscopic structures. For SEM images the GDC is on the left hand side with the AFL and ASL layers to the right. Cavities are observed for the room temperature laminates where delamination is causing gaps to form between the GDC and AFL layers in the interface region.
